issue.title: Landing continuation committed bob-cli and bob-mac-capture but stranded its bob-plugins and plans-sidecar edits (bob-cli-e6.land--4)

task_type_fields.impact: Silent loss of verified landing work across repos. A closed epic claimed plugin work that existed only as dirty files in a reusable workspace, while the vault ran unbranched code. A failed or partial commit gave no loud failure, and nothing re-surfaced the dirty obligations before the workspace was recycled.
task_type_fields.location: SASE host finalizer / commit obligations for opened linked repos and the plans sidecar in a monitor-continuation chain (bob-cli-e6.land--4, workspace bob-cli_16)
task_type_fields.repro:
Found by the bob-cli-e6 relaunch land agent (bob-cli-e6.land, run 20261030090721, 2026-10-30) while verifying the closed task-types epic bob-cli-e6. Not caused by bob-cli-e6's product work.

What happened (apollo, workspace bob-cli_16, times UTC):
1. The e6 landing ran as a chain: bob-cli-e6.land (planned tale land_task_types_epic.md) → land--code → land--mon → land--1 → mon-0 → land--2 → mon-1 → land--3 → mon-2 → land--4. land--1 and land--3 opened bob-plugins, bob-mac-capture, and the plans sidecar with `sase repo open` and edited all three (50 bob-plugins files; set plans/202610/task_types.md `status: done`).
2. land--4 closed bob-cli-e6 at 07:57:41 and wrote close note #5 claiming the plugin work (successor wiring, Pomodoro rename preview/tests, #TYPE geometry, type copy, planThemeChange retirement) was done and deployed. At 08:23 `sase repo log -a bob-cli-e6.land--4` shows it opened all three repos to "Inspect dirty ... files listed by the finalizer", so the obligations WERE surfaced (the bob-cli-dn discovery fix held).
3. Commits that resulted: bob-cli 3b0ffa0a (08:20) and bob-mac-capture 2f9a70a (08:35, SASE_BEAD bob-cli-e6). bob-plugins and the plans sidecar got NO commit. The bob-plugins edits stayed as dirty files in bob-cli_16 (staged + unstaged, 50 files, +570/-484) and task_types.md stayed `status: wip` on plans origin. `sase chat show --agent bob-cli-e6.land--4` finds no transcript.
4. The vault had been deployed from that dirty checkout at 07:57, so Obsidian ran code that existed on no branch. A later `bob plugins sync` from master would have silently reverted it.
5. bob-cli-ea.land (08:34) noticed the missing bob-plugins commit (ea note #3) and left it as e6 work. The relaunch lander rescued the diff with `git diff HEAD --binary` from bob-cli_16 at about 13:25. Minutes later bob-cli_16 was recycled and its sase/repos/linked/ directory vanished, so the rescue was nearly lost.

Unknown and worth determining: whether land--4 declared `commit` for bob-plugins and plans and the commit finalizer failed (bob-plugins origin moved 1295e52 → 5ba4683 at 08:40, so a push race is plausible), or whether the declaration omitted them. Look at land--4's final_context.json / commit_results.json in its run artifacts.

Repro idea: in a multi-continuation agent chain (monitor handoffs), open two linked repos plus the plans sidecar, edit all, and have the last continuation declare. Then check that every dirty opened repo gets a commit or a loud failure, and that a closed bead cannot claim work no branch carries.

issue.creation_reason: A multi-continuation land agent's finalizer surfaced dirty opened repos yet only two of four got commits, so a closed epic claimed unbranched plugin work and its plan status was lost; found by the bob-cli-e6 relaunch lander.

payload.description: Sibling stranding class: plan-propose handoff loses plan status and landing fixes; here a declared continuation lost plan status too
Phase finalization failure that discarded tracked edits; possible shared finalizer failure path
